VLNVerse NodeSet

The VLNVerse NodeSet (EnvVLNVerseNodeSet) exposes the VLNVerse Vision-and-Language Navigation environment — 262 kujiale (interior-design) USD scenes rendered by Isaac Sim 5.1, with fine/coarse instruction splits — as a standard AgentCanvas MDP env nodeset. It follows the env template's four-verb contract and mirrors the env_habitat three-layer shape (singleton manager + thin tool nodes + env panel), so agent graphs written for Habitat retarget to VLNVerse by swapping the node_type prefix.

Ported from the NavHarness VLNVerse stack (feat/env-vlnverse, merged into dev/coding-agent). Zero framework diff — nothing under agentcanvas/backend/app/** changed; the nodeset rides existing mechanisms (registry package discovery, auto_host, env panel, eval v2). AgentCanvas-native — no runtime dependency on a NavHarness/VLNVerse checkout: the Isaac seam is vendored, and both episode and scene data come from public Hugging Face repos.

1. Overview

Purpose

The VLNVerse NodeSet wraps the Isaac Sim 5.1 renderer over kujiale indoor scenes. It enables graphs to: - Step through navigation episodes with 1024² RGB + metric depth - Query agent position and orientation (egocentric proprioception only — no global pose leaks into the harness) - Control episode lifecycle (switch episodes, change dataset/split) from the Evaluate page's env panel - Render multi-view aligned RGB-D panoramas for waypoint-predictor / scene understanding

Architecture

The nodeset is a two-process design across an msgpack RPC seam — the reason it can auto-host in the repo's lightest conda env:

backend ── auto_host (ac-vlnverse conda env — lightest in the repo, no torch)
             VLNVerseEnvManager  (pure python: episodes / kinematics /
             occupancy collision / metrics — HabitatEnvManager name parity)
              └─ msgpack RPC over stdio ─▶ ~/isaacsim5.1/python.sh _isaac_worker.py
                                           (the ONLY file importing isaacsim/omni)

The manager layer imports only numpy / msgpack / PIL, so the registry can scan the module and auto-host it in ac-vlnverse without ever importing Isaac. Isaac Sim 5.1 stays behind the vendored standalone worker (_isaac_worker.py), launched by its own bundled python (~/isaacsim5.1/python.sh) — Isaac's python is never the server_python. This is the NavHarness SimBackend seam, vendored into the package.

VLNVerseEnvManager Singleton

The nodeset is organized around a singleton VLNVerseEnvManager that: - Maintains the single VLNVerse runtime + the Isaac worker subprocess - Enforces thread safety via a lock - Uses a dedicated single-threaded executor to serialize env state + worker RPC - Caches the rendered frame per pose (invalidated on every move / episode seat)

mgr = VLNVerseEnvManager.get()  # Always returns the same instance
result = mgr.step(action)  # reward / terminated / truncated / info

Method names deliberately mirror HabitatEnvManager — the auto_host POST /call/{fn} surface calls managers by method name, so keeping the names identical lets the coding-agent bridges / Human tab retarget from habitat to vlnverse (the driver's env_verb_prefix map supplies the env_vlnverse__ node namespace). All public methods are blocking and thread-safe; async code calls them via: 

await asyncio.get_running_loop().run_in_executor(mgr.executor, mgr.step, action)

Local vs Server Mode

Mode Execution Deployment When to use
Server Separate process ac-vlnverse env (Python 3.11) Default — the manager auto-hosts here; Isaac runs one hop further out
Auto-hosted Separate process Auto-detected via server_python Auto-routing; no manual ?mode=server

Because server_python resolves to the ac-vlnverse conda env (≠ the backend's interpreter), loading env_vlnverse auto-routes to server mode: the framework spins up an auto_host subprocess, which in turn spawns the Isaac 5.1 worker. Proxy nodes preserve the original node_type IDs (e.g. env_vlnverse__step_discrete), so graphs work identically regardless of routing. parallelism="replicated" — the env is stateful (per-worker scene + agent pose), so each worker owns an isolated Isaac instance.

2. Canvas Nodes

The nodeset ships six user-facing tools reusing the env-template suffixes. Unlike env_habitat, there are no separate internal ep_* episode-control nodes — the env panel drives episode lifecycle by calling manager methods (get_episodes_list, set_episode_by_index, switch_split) directly.

Node Type Display Name Category Input Ports Output Ports Description
env_vlnverse__reset VLNVerse: Reset environment trigger (ANY, optional) instruction (TEXT), episode_id (TEXT), scene_id (TEXT, kujiale scan) Ensure a live episode — emit metadata only, no observation. Episode placement is env panel-owned (set_episode); a done episode (canvas re-run) is re-armed in place, a live one (batch eval) read without disturbance. Rollover lives here, never in observe_*.
env_vlnverse__step_discrete VLNVerse: Step (discrete) environment action (ACTION, 0-3) reward (ANY), terminated (BOOL), truncated (BOOL), info (ANY) Advance one micro-tick: 0=STOP, 1=FORWARD 0.25 m, 2=LEFT +15°, 3=RIGHT −15°. Returns control signals only (pull perception from observe_egocentric).
env_vlnverse__step_hightolow VLNVerse: Step (HIGHTOLOW) environment angle (TEXT, rad), distance (TEXT, m), elevation (TEXT, DEGREES, optional) reward (ANY), terminated (BOOL), truncated (BOOL), info (ANY) Native VLNVerse MOVE macro — rotate by angle (radians, +CCW) then advance distance (m). STOP = angle=0, distance=0. Upstream unit quirk (test-pinned): elevation is DEGREES; defaults to 0 since all shipped episodes are single-floor.
env_vlnverse__observe_egocentric VLNVerse: Observe (egocentric) environment trigger (ANY, optional) rgb (IMAGE, 1024² 90° FOV), depth (DEPTH, metres float32), pose (POSE), intrinsics (ANY), raw_obs (ANY), instruction_text (TEXT) Pull the current first-person observation. Pure read — no lifecycle action; a finished episode observed again returns the terminal frame (re-arming is reset's job). Frame is cached per pose, so it renders at most once per move.
env_vlnverse__observe_panorama VLNVerse: Observe (panorama) environment trigger (ANY, optional) views (ANY), directions (TEXT), n_views (ANY), composite (IMAGE) Multi-view aligned RGB-D panorama. Config representation: views_rgbd (aligned RGB-D views, default — feeds the waypoint predictor) or composite (stitched grid image). dir_id 0 = current heading, increasing CCW (NavHarness strip convention). Expensive — one Isaac render + warmup per view; pull on demand.
env_vlnverse__evaluate VLNVerse: Evaluate evaluation trigger (TEXT, optional) metrics (METRICS), success (TEXT), spl (TEXT) Thin metric sink over the env's terminal state — pull SR/SPL/OS/nDTW/colrate without stepping. Read-only; works whether the episode ended by STOP (terminated) or step-budget truncation. Wire trigger from the loop's final_stop so it fires once.

This nodeset implements the gym-like env interface (4 verbs + pull perception). step_* nodes return no observation — perception is pulled via the observe_* family.

Notable Output Ports

  • pose (POSE): {"position": [x, y, z], "orientation": [qx, qy, qz, qw]} — emitted by observe_egocentric. Egocentric proprioception only.
  • intrinsics (ANY): {fx, fy, cx, cy, width, height}. fx = width/2 = 512 is correct — the worker sets the aperture to 2× focal (20 mm) → 90° horizontal FOV.
  • depth (DEPTH): metric depth in metres (float32). Isaac's +inf no-hit rays are clamped to a 20 m far-clip at the capture boundary, so no inf reaches the port.
  • terminated / truncated (BOOL): gym-style split — STOP/goal vs step-budget cutoff.
  • views (ANY) / composite (IMAGE): the two panorama representations. Each view carries {dir_id, heading_deg, rgb_base64, depth_base64, depth_raw_base64}.

3. Configuration

Initialization Parameters

When loading the nodeset via POST /api/components/nodesets/env_vlnverse/load, pass these kwargs in the request body:

{
  "dataset": "fine",
  "split": "val_unseen",
  "gpu_id": 0,
  "max_steps": 20
}
Parameter Type Default Description
dataset str fine fine (string instructions) or coarse (dict, formal field). Selects the final_splits/{dataset}_{split} episode file.
split str val_unseen Split suffix (see §4). A split switch swaps the episode list only — no Isaac reboot.
gpu_id int 0 CUDA device index for the Isaac worker.
max_steps int 20 Episode step budget. 20 = macro actions (HIGHTOLOW MLLM eval, NavHarness default). A discrete micro-step run (0.25 m / 15°) needs the habitat-style 500-step budget — override via $VLNVERSE_MAX_STEPS.

Success radius is per-episode (goals.radius, canonicalized at load); the module fallback when an episode carries no goal is 3.0 m.

Environment Variables

# ac-vlnverse conda python (auto-resolved; override if the env is elsewhere)
export VLNVERSE_PYTHON="python"

# Isaac Sim 5.1 launcher (the worker's bundled python)
export VLNVERSE_ISAAC_PYTHON="~/isaacsim5.1/python.sh"

# Data root holding raw_data/ + scene/ (default: repo data/vlnverse)
export VLNVERSE_DATA_ROOT="/path/to/vlnverse/data"

# Optional
export VLNVERSE_MAX_STEPS=500        # override step budget (500 for discrete micro-steps)
export VLNVERSE_HEADLESS=1          # 0 = show the Isaac viewport
export VLNVERSE_RENDERER="RaytracedLighting"
export VLNVERSE_SIM_SOCKET="/path/to.sock" # attach to a pre-started worker (socket backend)

Episode files are resolved from $VLNVERSE_DATA_ROOT/raw_data/final_splits/ (else the repo default data/vlnverse/raw_data); scenes from data/vlnverse/scene. On a dev machine install_ac_vlnverse.sh lays these down as symlinks to a NavHarness checkout for convenience — but a fresh machine populates them from Hugging Face (§4.1), so no checkout is required.

Node-Level Config: Panorama

The Panorama tool exposes two UI config fields:

ConfigField("representation", "select", default="views_rgbd",
            options=["views_rgbd", "composite"])
ConfigField("n_views", "slider", default=12, min=4, max=24, step=4)

views_rgbd returns per-direction aligned RGB-D (for the waypoint predictor); composite stitches a single grid image. n_views=12 → 30° steps.

4. Datasets: fine and coarse

The VLNVerse episode store is data/vlnverse/raw_data/final_splits/{dataset}_{split}.json[.gz]. There is no per-split YAML (unlike VLN-CE) — the sim config is identical across splits and only the episode list changes, so a split switch never reboots Isaac.

Dataset Instruction shape Notes
fine str Fine-grained step-by-step instruction (default).
coarse dict — formal field Coarse goal-level instruction.

Splits exposed in the panel/eval (display order, eval-relevant first): val_unseen, val, subset, subset_mini, mini, human, challenge, test, train. The final_splits/ dir also holds dialogue_subset / goalnav_subset / long_horizon* / interactive_subset families (different task semantics) and *.withheld challenge twins (goals=None, unscorable) — everything not in the list above is out of contract and fenced off.

Episode geometry: all 16,867 shipped episodes are single-floor (z ≡ 0 verified), which is why step_hightolow.elevation defaults to 0 and floor changes never arise. Scenes are 262 kujiale interior-design USDs.

4.1 Data Download

Two Hugging Face fetchers populate data/vlnverse/ — episodes and scenes live in separate repos and share the $VLNVERSE_DATA_ROOT contract:

# Episodes — 8 small .json.gz splits (~a few MB), HF Eyz/VLNVerse_data
python3 scripts/data/fetch_episodes_vlnverse.py             # all splits
python3 scripts/data/fetch_episodes_vlnverse.py --list

# Scenes — 262 kujiale USDs (~80 GB), HF Eyz/VLNVerse_scene (rate-limit backoff)
python3 scripts/data/fetch_scenes_vlnverse.py
bash scripts/data/fetch_scenes_vlnverse_loop.sh      # resume loop for the 80 GB pull

Split coverage caveat: the HF episode repo ships only the four canonical splits per dataset (train / val / val_unseen / test). Extra splits the panel can enumerate (challenge / human / subset / mini …) exist only in a NavHarness checkout, not on HF — they are not needed for standard eval. The episode fetcher also deliberately excludes the upstream traj_data/ tree (~47k per-episode recordings) the nodeset does not use.

5. Env Panel Integration

The VLNVerse NodeSet declares a VLNVerseEnvPanel (a BaseEnvPanel subclass) as a class-level attribute (env_panel = VLNVerseEnvPanel). This lets the canvas Evaluate page manage episodes uniformly across all environments.

Three-Field Cascade (Dataset → Split → Episode)

The panel exposes a three-field cascade mirroring HabitatEnvPanel:

  • dataset — fine or coarse. Changing resets split and episode_index and re-routes the episode file.
  • split — dataset-conditional list via _dataset_splits(dataset) (discovered from the on-disk final_splits/ files). Changing triggers _switch_split, which swaps the episode list — cheap: no Isaac reboot, the scene switches lazily on episode seating.
  • episode_index — index into the currently loaded dataset/split; the label shows {index}: {scene_id}.

Each field change emits a signal side-effect with signal_name="episode_reset", so any lifetime="episode" state container clears downstream. This matches the Habitat/MP3D panel contract, so agent graphs bind state lifetimes without knowing which simulator is active.

How It Works

  1. Evaluate page calls on_load() → datasets + splits + current state (or an “environment not initialized / server mode” message when the manager singleton is empty)
  2. User selects an episode → on_field_change("episode_index", …) arms the index and emits episode_reset
  3. on_action("play") calls mgr.set_episode_by_index(…) and starts the run
  4. Graph continues; agent navigates in the new episode

Server-mode limitation: when the env runs in a spawned subprocess, the local manager singleton is empty by design (no control-plane bridge yet), so the panel reports episode control as unavailable and shows a message. Batch eval seats episodes through the driver, not this panel.

6. Installation & Usage

From Zero (fresh machine)

# 1. Isaac Sim 5.1 — MANUAL prerequisite (tens of GB), e.g. under ~/isaacsim5.1
#    https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/ (workstation install)

# 2. Create the ac-vlnverse conda env (lightest in the repo — no torch) + verify Isaac
bash scripts/install/install_ac_vlnverse.sh

# 3. Fetch data from Hugging Face (no NavHarness checkout needed)
python3 scripts/data/fetch_episodes_vlnverse.py    # episodes (~few MB)
python3 scripts/data/fetch_scenes_vlnverse.py      # scenes (~80 GB)

The install script only verifies Isaac Sim (it is a manual prereq) and, if $VLNVERSE_DATA_ROOT points at an existing store, symlinks it instead of downloading.

Loading the NodeSet

POST /api/components/nodesets/env_vlnverse/load

server_python resolves to ac-vlnverse, so this auto-routes to server mode; the Isaac worker boots on first episode seat.

Typical Graph Workflow

1. Load VLNVerse nodeset  (env panel: pick dataset / split / episode)
   ↓
2. VLNVerse: Reset → instruction + episode_id + scene_id
   ↓
3. Loop:
   - VLNVerse: Observe (egocentric) → RGB + depth + pose + instruction_text
   - [Policy / reasoning node] → decide action
   - VLNVerse: Step (hightolow)  angle,distance   (or Step discrete 0-3)
   - [Iterate; break on terminated/truncated]
   ↓
4. VLNVerse: Evaluate → SR / SPL / nDTW / colrate

Error Handling

  • “Environment not initialized”: load env_vlnverse from the NodeSet Manager first.
  • Panel shows “server mode — episode control not supported”: expected; the env is in a subprocess. Use batch eval (driver seats episodes) or run the panel against a local manager.
  • Worker boot hangs: the Isaac launcher prints a conda warning to stdout that a naive parent misreads as a giant frame length — the seam guards against it with a STDIO_MAGIC preamble + dup2 fd1 redirect + CONDA_* scrub. If it still hangs, run the worker's --check self-test.
  • Missing scenes/episodes: run the two fetchers, or point $VLNVERSE_DATA_ROOT at an existing store.

Performance Considerations

  • Scene switch: ~20–30 s cold (USD load + stabilize) / ~1.2 s warm (omniverse cache). default_per_step_budget_sec=60 leaves headroom for cross-scene episode switches during batch eval.
  • Panorama: n_views=12 is 12 Isaac renders with warmup — expensive; use fewer views for quick iteration.
  • Frame caching: the manager caches the rendered frame per pose, so repeated observe_egocentric calls between moves are free.
  • VRAM: RTX RaytracedLighting steady state ≈ 6 GB per worker (author preset).
